thread:
maria: Pushed an nsys + perfetto sampling run for the INT8 candidate on xg-4 (A100s). Upload at https://perfetto.google.cn/trace?token=abc123 (short link).
aj: Quick summary? what jumped out?
maria: High-level: 95th latency up ~28% vs FP8 baseline. Throughput similar, but tail latency and CPU-GPU syncs worse.
leo: Did you collect kernel timelines? any dequant hotspots?
maria: Yes — NVTX ranges + nsys timeline shows a big region labeled `dequant_cuda` chaining into `matmul_int8_fused` with repeated host-device memcpy bursts. `dequant_cuda` accounts for ~42% of token time on median, ~55% on the tail.
catherine: That's huge. Is that the per-token dequant (INT8->FP32) we added in the runtime path?
maria: Exactly. The quantized model uses int8 kernels but we still dequant for softmax + rotary and some fused ops. The NVTX trace highlights many small `cudaMemcpyAsync` (4-16KB) between device and host around KV cache refresh.
aj: Small async memcopies = PCIe roundtrips. Are we falling back to CPU for certain ops?
maria: Not exactly fallback, but the current kernel selection emits a host-side dequant path for attention bias computation. The timeline shows `cudaMemcpyAsync` -> `host_dequant_do_work` -> `cudaMemcpyAsync` back. That sequence multiplies with larger batch sizes.
leo: Which batching heuristic are you running? max_batch=32, microbatch=4?
maria: Running the heuristic from last week: dynamic batch up to 48, microbatch=8, batching window 8ms. The high batching window + big max_batch increases concurrency but exacerbates small copy storms for queries hitting cold KV shards.
catherine: So two factors: dequant-host-copy pattern and larger batches causing more concurrent small memcpys. Agree. Any memory staging (pinned) used?
maria: Yes pinned, but NVTX shows host CPU stalls waiting on those copies — the host-side dequant is CPU-bound (single-threaded in our path).
aj: Can you paste the nsys summary (top kernels)?
maria: Sure, excerpt: ```
Kernel            Calls   GPU Time(ms)   %Time
dequant_cuda      12      342.8           42.1
matmul_int8_fused 12      180.3           22.1
softmax_fp32      12      78.9            9.7
cudaMemcpyAsync   96      64.2            7.9
kv_prefetch       24      46.0            5.6
other             -       40.0            4.6
```
leo: Interesting that `matmul_int8_fused` is fast but `dequant_cuda` dominates. Could we fuse dequant into matmul or implement device-side dequant+softmax?
maria: We prototyped a fused kernel last month but saw correctness edge cases for rotary. FP8 path had a working fused softmax+rotary; INT8 path didn't because scale factors differ.
leo: What about moving dequant to a CUDA kernel (device-side) instead of host? That should eliminate memcpys.
maria: Agreed. Device-side dequant halves the latency in a microbenchmark. Also we can change kernel selection rule to prefer `matmul_int8_deq_fused` when sequence_length <= 1024 and batch < 24.
aj: Could we change batching heuristic instead: reduce batching_window to 4ms or cap max_batch per shard to 24 to avoid copy storms?
maria: Yes. I ran a quick ablation: lowering batching_window from 8ms->4ms reduces concurrent memcpy bursts by ~35% and 95th latency drops from 230ms -> 195ms. Device-side dequant patch further drops 95th to 160ms.
catherine: Any accuracy numbers on INT8 vs FP8? we need the perf/quality tradeoff.
maria: Eval on our prompt suite: int8 quant + per-channel calibration yields avg perplexity delta +0.32% and answer-EM drop 0.26%. FP8 baseline delta is ~+0.05%.
leo: So INT8 slightly worse but within SLO for many workloads. For retrieval rerankers maybe ok. For chat L7 customers maybe not.
aj: Next steps? prioritize device-side dequant kernel + batching heuristic change as low-risk mitigation.
maria: I filed a runtime ticket: RUNTIME-2483 (device dequant prototype + kernel selection rule). Also RUNTIME-2484 for batching heuristic knob and staged rollout on canary capacity.
perf-bot: nsys profile uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/1768765432_int8_trace.nsys (size 78MB).
deploy-bot: Canary patch queued for dedicated pool `dedicated-prod-eu` (tag: deq-device-2026-03).
aj: For the patch, add a flag to force device-deq so we can test correctness across rotary/rope/flash-attn combos.
maria: Will add unit tests + an eval run with 2500 prompts. Also will instrument KV prefetch to add an atomic backoff so we don't spawn >16 concurrent prefetch memcpys per GPU.
catherine: Sounds good. If device deq lands, we should update Optimize recommendations (quant profiles) to prefer INT8 with device-deq enabled for throughput-sensitive deployments.
maria: Agreed. I'll attach perfetto URL with NVTX ranges + the annotated timeline in the ticket. Plan: patch -> canary -> perf sample -> roll.
leo: Thanks, this is actionable. :thumbsup:
maria: Thanks all, starting the device-kernel PR now.
